test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 28 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dealer wants to make a 20% profit on a smart watch that costs him ₹1,575. To attract customers, he plans to offer a 10% discount on the listed price. At what price should he list the smart watch to achieve his desired profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct ratio formula between Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP):

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

MP ÷ 1575 = (100 + 20) ÷ (100 − 10)

MP ÷ 1575 = 120 ÷ 90 = 4 ÷ 3

MP = 1575 × 4 ÷ 3 = 525 × 4 = 2100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,575

⇒ Profit = 20%

⇒ Discount = 10%

Formula Used:

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 CP = 1575
 
 
 SP = 1890
 
 
 MP = 2100
 
 

 +20% Profit
 
 

 -10% Discount

 Marked Price = ₹2100

Calculations:

⇒ SP = 1575 × (100 + 20) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 1575 × 1.2 = ₹1,890

⇒ MP = 1890 × 100 ÷ (100 − 10)

⇒ MP = 1890 × 100 ÷ 90

⇒ MP = 1890 × 10 ÷ 9

⇒ MP = 210 × 10 = ₹2,100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct MP to CP Ratio

The most efficient way to link Marked Price and Cost Price without calculating Selling Price is: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective single discount is calculated as: a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Markup Percentage

Markup indicates how much above the cost price the product is listed. Markup % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.
